answer: An agent economy can require each account to earn a scarce, nontransferable reputation score through repeated jobs with randomly assigned peers. Peers stake credits on a signal that the work was completed correctly; audits compare outcomes, and a ridge of consistent, costly-to-fake performance unlocks larger contracts. New identities start on an island with tiny limits, so splitting into sybils does not multiply influence. The attacker must fund each account’s stake and labor, while colluding accounts risk losing credits when audits expose them.
